title: An Entropy-Aware Adaptive Face–Voice Biometric Fusion Using Lipschitz-Bounded Attention Mechanism
content: Multimodal biometric fusion is commonly justified by the claim that combining modalities compensates for the degradation of any single one, yet attention-based fusion layers learn the reallocation of trust implicitly and offer no guarantee that the fused representation is stable when one embedding is perturbed. This paper introduces Entropy-Aware Adaptive Fusion (EAAF), a Lipschitz-bounded attention mechanism for face–voice fusion whose attention logits are penalised by the Shannon entropy of the softmax-normalised magnitude spectrum of each embedding, so that a less informative modality receives less weight. Three results are proved directly: First, the weights are Lipschitz and confined to a closed sub-interval of \((0, 1)\), thus no modality can be switched off; Second, the fused representation is Lipschitz with an explicit constant set by the entropy weight and the softmax temperature; and Third, with frozen encoders, stochastic gradient descent with a horizon-scaled cosine step attains the \(O(1/\sqrt{T})\) stationarity rate. On chimeric face–voice identities from LFW, MS1M-RetinaFace and VoxCeleb1&2, EAAF reaches equal error rates of 0.93% (clean) and 1.17% (12 dB acoustic noise), against 1.94% and 2.37% for co-attention, while adding 514 parameters and 0.53% inference overhead. All values are outputs of a calibrated computational experiment; empirical replication is in progress.
